title: Console MVP telemetry floorplan — targeted cuts and acceptance checklist
creator: Lena Morrison
description: Goal: Deliver a minimal, production-safe telemetry surface for Redwood Console that provides actionable signals for latency, cost, and errors while keeping ingestion and UI complexity low. This ticket defines the cuts we will make to dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown to meet the MVP date and outlines acceptance criteria and rollback guardrails. Background: Initial PRD requested rich per-route heatmaps, full waterfall traces for every error, and per-token cost attribution in the UI. Engineering estimates showed a 2x ingestion and storage delta and >30% frontend complexity increase. We must reduce scope to ship a usable, maintainable MVP that covers most operator workflows.
rationale: Prioritize signals that improve incident TTR (time to recovery): error rates, p50/p95 latency by service/route, and gross cost trend
Defer high-cardinality, high-ingest features (per-user token attribution, per-request full KV traces) to post-MVP because of backend cost and querying complexity
Keep UI surface predictable: prefer aggregated charts and sampled drilldowns rather than full-fidelity live streams
scope_removed: Per-request full waterfall traces for all requests — replace with sampled trace snapshots (1% sample) and on-demand ad hoc capture
Realtime per-route heatmap (second-granularity) — replace with 1-minute rollup and anomaly markers
Token-level cost attribution in the Console — replace with coarse bucketed cost categories (model, compute, storage) and per-route average cost
Long retention for detailed diagnostics (defer >90d detailed retention; retain aggregates for 90d, detail for 14d)
Live streaming of every console session's telemetry to the UI (defer until streaming tier established)
scope_included: Dashboard: top-line telemetry card set (errors, p50/p95 latency, request rate, gross cost) per-route and per-model
Tracing: sampled trace snapshots (1% default) with ability to increase sampling for a specific route for 1 hour
Cost: coarse breakdown by category (model usage, GPU compute, other infra) with per-route average cost and 7/30-day trend
Rollouts: add basic rollout impact card showing metrics delta for canary vs baseline
Acceptance tests and basic alerting integration for SLO regression and cost spike detection
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard surfaces: Errors, Request Rate, p50 and p95 latency, and Gross Cost are visible and filterable by route and model
Sampled traces open from any dashboard row and render within 2s for sampled traces; ability to increase sampling to 100% for targeted 1-hour window via toggle
Cost page shows model/compute/infra buckets and per-route average cost; numbers reconcile within 5% to billing exports for the last 7 days
Ingestion pipeline limit: telemetry ingestion rate remains within the planned budget (<= baseline + 25%); engineering signs off on cost estimate
Telemetry UI renders with <150ms time-to-first-paint for the main dashboard card set on a mid-tier laptop (Chrome)
Runbook & rollback: documented rollback steps for telemetry ingest/config changes; can disable sampling and revert to aggregates within 30 minutes
Basic alerts: SLO regression and cost spike detection rules are created and firing during QA scenarios
rollout_plan: Phase 0 — Feature flag behind `console.telemetry.mvp` (internal only). Smoke test ingest and UI with canary customers
Phase 1 — Enable for 10% of orgs; monitor ingestion, UI performance, and cost; run reconciliation checks with billing exports
Phase 2 — Expand to 50% orgs with opt-in for traced sampling controls; collect feedback and bug fixes
Phase 3 — Full launch after 2 weeks of stable metrics and sign-off from Eng/Infra/SSO/Security
risks: Under-sampling could miss root causes for low-volume production errors — mitigated by on-demand increased sampling and targeted capture
Cost estimates might be optimistic if adoption concentrates on high-cardinality routes — mitigation: throttle ingestion and degrade to aggregates automatically
UX may be confusing if drilldowns return sparse data — mitigation: add clear UX copy and empty-state guidance
Backend query latency for aggregated metrics could impact dashboard performance — mitigation: precompute rollups and cache recent windows
decision_history: 2026-02-20: PM + Eng agreed to sample traces by default (1%) and provide a temporary targeted sampling toggle instead of shipping full tracing for every request (Lena Morrison, Marco Li)
2026-02-24: Removed per-token cost breakdown from MVP after infra cost analysis showed 2.1x storage delta (Diego Ramirez, Avery Collins)
2026-02-26: Chose 1-minute rollups for route heatmaps (vs 5-min) to balance fidelity and ingest cost — accepted by data infra (Sana Patel)
2026-03-03: Added rollback guard to disable sampling if ingestion spikes > 40% of expected budget (Engineering Ops)
technical_notes: Backend: use existing metrics proxy with additional rollup layer; cost categories emitted at ingestion time to avoid post-aggregation joins
Tracing: leverage the new tracing-lite pipeline that stores spans in compressed form for sampled traces; capture limited KV snapshot for sampled traces only
Storage/Retention: keep detailed sampled traces for 14 days, aggregated rollups for 90 days
Frontend: avoid client-side heavy rendering; load primary card set first and lazy-load drilldowns
